label: Slot type
summary: Going by its name, the type of an agent slot.
details: The game lists no return type and no use of it on an agent slot. Texts use the same name on artifacts, to show the artifact's slot type, which is only a hint.

label: The slot itself
summary: Going by its name and the way `Character.Self` is used elsewhere, gives the agent slot itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types, for example `CHARACTER.Self` passed into a call.

label: The slot type itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the agent slot type itself as a reference, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way in GUI files, which is a hint from another type.

label: Description
summary: The description text of an agent slot type.
details: The game's shared tooltip file shows it as the text of a tooltip box.

label: Name
summary: Going by its name, the display name of an agent slot type, with its hover tooltip.
details: The same function name gives a name on many other types. Vanilla shows no line using it on an agent slot type itself. That it carries a hover tooltip is only inferred from the sibling GetNameNoTooltip.

label: Name without tooltip
summary: The name of an agent slot type as plain text, without the hover tooltip that the normal name carries.
details: The game's shared tooltip file uses it as a text line.

label: The slot type itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the agent slot type itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types, for example `Character.Self` passed to a function.

label: The alliance itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the alliance info itself as a reference, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Character
summary: The character the alliance entry is about.
details: The game's interaction window file uses it as the data source of a part of the window that shows a character. Which of the two allied characters it is, the input does not say.

label: Military info
summary: The military information of the alliance entry, used as the data source of a part of the interaction window.
details: What exactly the military info holds is not shown in the input.

label: The alliance itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the alliance info itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types.

label: The ally list itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the ally list part of the window itself as a reference, so it can be passed on.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Close ally list
summary: Closes the ally list part of the war declaration window.
details: The war declaration window calls it when a button is clicked. It does not return a value.

label: Ally list
summary: The list of allies shown in the ally list part of the war declaration window.
details: The window uses it as the data source of a list.

label: Header title
summary: The title text shown at the top of the ally list in the war declaration window.

label: Is shown
summary: Whether the ally list part of the war declaration window is currently open.
details: The window uses it to show or hide that part.

label: The ally list itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the ally list part itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types.

label: The anchor itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the anchor item itself as a reference, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Anchor index as text
summary: Going by its name, the position number of an anchor (a point on a spline) written as text.
details: Its one use shows it as text in the map editor's spline inspector.

label: Display text
summary: Going by its name, the text shown for an anchor entry.
details: Its one use shows it as text in the map editor's spline inspector.

label: Index validator
summary: Going by its name, the check that decides which anchor numbers can be typed in.
details: Its one use is as the text validator of an input in the map editor's spline inspector. The game gives no return type.

label: Tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text of an anchor entry.
details: Its one use is as a tooltip in the map editor's spline inspector.

label: Is expanded
summary: Going by its name, whether an anchor entry is opened up.
details: Its one use shows or hides part of the map editor's spline inspector.

label: Is locked
summary: Going by its name, whether an anchor is locked.
details: Its one use sets whether a checkbox in the map editor's spline inspector is ticked.

label: The anchor itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the anchor item itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types.

label: Set anchor index
summary: Going by its name, takes over the anchor number typed in.
details: Its one use runs it when editing of an input in the map editor's spline inspector is finished. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle expanded
summary: Going by its name, opens an anchor entry if it is closed and closes it if it is open.
details: Its one use is a button click in the map editor's spline inspector. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle lock
summary: Going by its name, locks an anchor if it is unlocked and unlocks it if it is locked.
details: Its one use is a button click in the map editor's spline inspector. It returns nothing.

label: The group item itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the animation test group item itself as a reference, so it can be passed on.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Name
summary: The name of an animation group in the animation test window's list.
details: This is a debug window of the game. The list rows show this name as their text.

label: The group item itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the animation test group item itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types.

label: The window itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the animation test window itself as a reference, so it can be passed on.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Animation groups
summary: The list of animation groups shown in the animation test window.
details: The window uses it as the data source of its list. This is a debug window of the game.

label: Selected animation group
summary: Going by its name, the name of the animation group picked in the animation test window.
details: It returns text. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Selected group index
summary: The list position of the animation group that is picked in the animation test window.
details: It returns a pair of whole numbers. The window uses it as the selected entry of its list.

label: The window itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the animation test window itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types.

label: Select animation group
summary: Picks an animation group in the animation test window.
details: The window calls it when the selection in its list changes. It returns nothing.

label: The application itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the application object itself as a reference, so it can be passed on.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Quit game
summary: Going by its name, quits the game.
details: It returns nothing. The game documents nothing more and vanilla never uses it.

label: The application itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the application object itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types.

label: The window itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the court position appointment window itself as a reference, so it can be passed on.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Appoint selected courtier
summary: Appoints the courtier picked in the window to the court position.
details: The appointment window calls it when a button is clicked. It returns nothing.

label: Appointing revoke text
summary: Going by its name and the tooltip it is used in, the text about what is revoked as a consequence of appointing someone to the position.
details: The game shows it in a tooltip whose key names the consequence of an appointment. The input does not show the actual wording.

label: Can show character
summary: Going by its name, whether a given character may be shown in the appointment window's list.
details: It takes one argument, a character, and returns yes or no. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The character to check. The game does not document the argument; by its name it is a character.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the court position appointment window.
details: The window's buttons call it on click. It returns nothing.

label: AI candidate score
summary: The score the AI would give a character as a candidate for the court position.
details: Vanilla shows it in a line starting with 'AI Score', with no decimals.

label: Aptitude text
summary: The text describing how well a character suits the court position.
details: The game's text shows it after the word aptitude.

label: Aptitude tooltip
summary: The tooltip data that explains a character's aptitude for the court position.
details: The window uses it as the data source of a tooltip.

fields.name: character
fields.text: The candidate the tooltip is about.

label: Court
summary: The court the position belongs to.
details: The window uses it as the data source of the parts that show the court.

label: Court owner
summary: The owner of the court the position is in.
details: The window uses it as the data source of the parts that show that character.

label: Position to replace
summary: The court position that would be replaced, when the window is used to replace someone.
details: A text uses it to name the current holder of the position being replaced.

label: Court position type
summary: The type of court position the window is about.
details: The window uses it as a data source, and also asks it whether the position is travel related.

label: Court effects of position
summary: Going by its name, the text about the modifier the position gives to the court owner's court.
details: The game's text shows it under a heading about effects on the court owner's realm. What 'liege' means here is not stated in the input.

fields.name: position type
fields.text: Not documented; by its name the kind of position to describe.
fields.values: a court position type (by its name)

label: Liege effects of position
summary: Going by its name, the text about the modifier the position gives to its liege.
details: The window shows it as a text line. Vanilla passes it a character (`Character.Self`), although the name speaks of a position type.

label: Liege effects of selection
summary: Going by its name, the text about the modifier the selected candidate gives to the liege.
details: The window shows it as a text line.

label: Opinion bonus of selection
summary: The opinion bonus shown for the selected candidate in the appointment window.
details: It returns a whole number. The game's text shows it after the word opinion and the selected character's name. The input does not say who holds the opinion of whom.

label: Position name
summary: The name of the court position, with its hover tooltip.
details: Used in headers such as appoint or replace. That it carries a hover tooltip is only inferred from the sibling GetPositionNameNoTooltip.

label: Position name, plain
summary: The name of the court position as plain text, without a hover tooltip.

label: Selected character
summary: The character currently picked in the appointment window.
details: Texts use it to show the candidate's name. The window checks whether anyone is picked with `HasSelectedCharacter`.

label: Has selected character
summary: Whether a character is currently picked in the appointment window.
details: The window uses it to enable and show its confirm parts.

label: Is appointing new
summary: Going by its name, whether the window is appointing to a position as new.
details: The window shows parts only in this mode. The input does not describe the mode further.

label: Is item selected
summary: Whether a given list row is the one picked in the window.
details: The window uses it to draw the row as pressed.

label: Is replacing
summary: Going by its name, whether the window is replacing a position's holder.
details: The window shows parts only in this mode. The input does not describe the mode further.

label: Replace revoke text
summary: Going by its name and the tooltip it is used in, the text about what is revoked as a consequence of replacing the current holder.
details: The game shows it in a tooltip whose key names the consequence of revoking. The input does not show the actual wording.

label: Revoke position
summary: Going by its name, takes the court position away from its holder.
details: The window calls it from a button click. It returns nothing.

label: The window itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the appointment window itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types.

label: The window itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the tax collector appointment window itself as a reference, so it can be passed on.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Appoint character
summary: Appoints the picked character as tax collector.
details: The window calls it from a button click. It returns nothing.

label: Close window
summary: Closes the tax collector appointment window.
details: A button calls it on click. It returns nothing.

label: Levy change
summary: Going by its name, the change in levy that appointing the picked character would cause.
details: The window uses it as a data source for its display. The input does not say more about the form of the value.

label: Potential tax collectors
summary: The list of characters who can be appointed as tax collector.
details: The window uses it as the data source of its candidate list.

label: Selected character
summary: The character currently picked in the window.
details: The window uses it as the data source of the parts that show that character.

label: Tax change
summary: Going by its name, the change in tax income that appointing the picked character would cause.
details: The window uses it as a data source for its display. The input does not say more about the form of the value.

label: Current tax collector
summary: The character who is now tax collector of the slot.
details: A text uses it to name who would be fired when replacing.

label: Tax slot
summary: The tax slot the window is about.
details: The window uses it as a data source, and a text asks it for the effect of firing.

label: Taxpayer limit change
summary: Going by its name, the change in the taxpayer limit that appointing the picked character would cause.
details: The window uses it as a data source for its display. The input does not say more about the form of the value.

label: Has selected character
summary: Whether a character is currently picked in the window.
details: The window uses it to show or hide parts, also with `Not`.

label: Has tax collector
summary: Whether the slot already has a tax collector.
details: The window shows different parts depending on it.

label: Is character selected
summary: Whether a given list row is the character picked in the window.
details: The window uses it to draw the row as pressed.

label: Is current tax collector
summary: Whether a given character is the present tax collector of the slot.
details: The window uses it with `Not` to show a part only for other characters.

label: Remove tax collector
summary: Removes the present tax collector from the slot.
details: A button calls it on click. It returns nothing.

label: The window itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the tax collector window itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types.

label: The list itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the appointment candidate list itself as a reference, so it can be passed on.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Appointment score
summary: The appointment score of the candidate at a given list position.
details: Texts show it as the candidate score, with no decimals.

fields.name: index
fields.text: The row's position in the list.

label: Governor efficiency
summary: Going by its name, how efficient the candidate at a given list position would be as governor.
details: It returns a number. Vanilla never uses it.

fields.name: index
fields.text: The row's position in the list (by its name).

label: Merit item
summary: The merit entry of the candidate at a given list position.
details: The title appointment window uses it as the data source of a part of the window for that candidate.

fields.name: index
fields.text: The row's position in the list.

label: Succession order
summary: The place of the candidate at a given list position in the order of succession.
details: It returns a whole number. A text shows it as the rank.

fields.name: index
fields.text: The row's position in the list.

label: The list itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the candidate list itself, so it can be handed on as an argument.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `.Self` on other types.

label: The army itself
summary: Going by its name, gives the army itself as a reference, so it can be passed on to another function.
details: The game documents nothing more. Vanilla only shows `PdxGuiWidget.AccessSelf` used that way, which is a hint from another type.

label: Acclaimed knights breakdown
summary: The tooltip text that breaks down the acclaimed knights in the army.
details: The army window shows it as a tooltip.

label: Quality level
summary: Going by its name, the quality level of the army as a whole number.
details: Vanilla uses the same name on an army's composition to pick a map icon frame, which is only a hint.

label: Commander is owner
summary: Whether the army's commander is the army's owner.
details: The army window uses it to show or hide parts.

label: Custom text
summary: Going by its name, runs one of the game's custom text entries with the army as its subject.
details: It takes one argument and returns text. Vanilla shows the same name often on other types, but no line on an army.

fields.name: name
fields.text: The name of the custom text.

label: AI order description
summary: The text describing what order the AI has given the army.
details: The army window and the shared tooltip show it as text.

label: Activity frame
summary: Going by its name, the number of the picture frame that shows what the army is doing.
details: It returns a whole number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: AI coordinator id
summary: The number of the AI coordinator that handles the army.
details: The shared tooltip shows it in a plain text line.

label: AI sub stack id
summary: The number of the AI sub unit stack the army belongs to.
details: The shared tooltip shows it in a plain text line beside the stack number.

label: AI stack id
summary: The number of the AI unit stack the army belongs to.
details: The shared tooltip shows it in a plain text line.

label: Army attrition
summary: How many soldiers the army loses to attrition each month.
details: It returns a whole number. The army tooltip shows it with a sign, per month. Attrition is the loss of troops from hard conditions.

label: Attrition breakdown
summary: Going by its name, a text listing the causes of the army's attrition.
details: It returns text. Vanilla never uses it; the percentage version is used instead.

label: Attrition breakdown (percent)
summary: A text listing the causes of the army's attrition, in percent.
details: It follows the monthly attrition line in the army tooltip.

label: Attrition percentage
summary: The share of the army lost to attrition each month, in percent.
details: The army's tooltips show it as a monthly percentage.

label: Army id
summary: The internal number of the army.
details: The shared tooltip shows it in a plain text line beside the unit number.

label: Quality name
summary: Going by its name, the name of the army's quality level.
details: It returns text. Vanilla uses the same name on an army composition as a tooltip, which is only a hint.

label: Status illustration
summary: The picture that shows the army's status in the army window.
details: The window uses it as a texture.

label: Status icon
summary: The icon that shows the army's status in the outliner on the side of the screen.

label: Status tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the army's status in the outliner.

label: Barter loot
summary: How much loot the army carries from a barter mission.
details: The army's tooltips show it next to a loot icon. Another text gives the most the army can carry.

label: Barter mission
summary: The barter mission the army is on.
details: The army window uses it as the data source of the parts about that mission.

label: Combat prediction
summary: Going by its name, the text predicting how a combat of the army would go, for a tooltip.
details: It returns text. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Commander
summary: The character who commands the army.
details: The outliner uses it as the data source of the parts that show the commander.

label: Commander tooltip
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text about the army's commander.
details: It returns text. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Composition
summary: The make-up of the army, the troops it consists of.
details: The outliner and the army window use it as the data source for parts that show the troops.

label: Debug AI info
summary: A debug text with information about how the AI handles the army.
details: The shared tooltip shows it.

label: Description
summary: Going by its name, the description text of the army.
details: It returns text. Vanilla shows no line using it on an army. The same name on a building gives its description, which is only a hint.

label: Disembark penalty days
summary: Going by its name, the number of days the army stays under the disembark penalty.
details: It returns a whole number. A map icon text mentions being recently disembarked, which fits but is not shown as using this function.

label: Embark info
summary: The tooltip text about the army boarding ships.
details: The shared tooltip shows it as text.

label: Event troops and war
summary: Going by its name, the tooltip text about event troops of the army and the war they belong to.
details: It returns text. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Gathering days left
summary: How many days the army still needs to finish gathering.
details: It returns a whole number. Texts show it as days left.

label: Gathering progress
summary: How far the army's gathering has come, as a number for a progress bar.
details: The map icons and the army window use it as the value of a bar. It is a decimal number.

label: Location
summary: The place where the army currently is.
details: The army window follows it to the siege there, so the place can hold a siege.

label: Loot cap
summary: The most loot the army can carry.
details: The raid and barter tooltips show it after the amount carried.

label: Max soldiers
summary: Going by its name, the army's maximum soldier count written as text.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Movement info
summary: The tooltip text about how the army is moving.
details: The army window and the shared tooltip show it.

label: Movement progress
summary: Going by its name, how far along its current move the army is, as a ratio.
details: It returns a decimal number. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Name
summary: The name of the army, with its hover tooltip.
details: A text uses it to show which army is followed. That it carries a hover tooltip is only inferred from the sibling GetNameNoTooltip.

label: Name, plain
summary: The name of the army as plain text, without a hover tooltip.
details: The outliner and the army window use it as a heading.

label: Acclaimed knights
summary: The number of acclaimed knights in the army.
details: It returns a whole number shown in the army window.

label: Orders
summary: The orders that can be given to the army.
details: The army window takes commands from it, for example to halt the army, and checks first whether they are allowed.

label: Owner
summary: The character who owns the army.
details: The army window shows that character and can check the owner's settings, for example the AI setting for assigning commanders.

label: Raid
summary: The raid the army is carrying out.
details: The army window uses it as the data source of the raid parts.

label: Raid intent
summary: Going by its name, what the army intends to get from a raid.
details: Vanilla uses the same name on the army window, not on the army itself, so this is only a hint.

label: Raid loot
summary: How much loot the army carries from raiding.
details: The army's tooltips show it next to a loot icon, and another text gives the most the army can carry.

label: Fleet raising cost
summary: Going by its name, what it costs to raise a fleet for the army.
details: It takes one argument and returns a number. The input does not say what the argument is. Vanilla never uses it.

label: Soldier count
summary: The number of soldiers in the army.
details: Vanilla's army window shows it as a number for the selected army.

label: Soldier count text
summary: The number of soldiers in the army, written as text.
details: The outliner shows it as a line of text.

label: Special status
summary: Going by its name, a text naming a special status of the army.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Supply description
summary: Going by its name, the text describing the army's supplies.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Supply info
summary: The tooltip text about the army's supplies.
details: The shared tooltip shows it as text.

label: Supply state tooltip
summary: The tooltip text that explains the army's supply state.
details: The army window shows it as a tooltip.

label: Army supplies (whole)
summary: Going by its name, the army's supplies cut to a whole number.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Supply change (whole)
summary: Going by its name, the change in the army's supplies cut to a whole number.
details: Vanilla never uses it.

label: Type name
summary: The name of the kind of unit the army is.
details: A map tooltip header shows it after the army's identifier.

label: AI order icon
summary: The icon that shows the order the AI has given the army.
details: The map icons use it as a texture.

label: Unit id
summary: The internal number of the army's unit.
details: The shared tooltip shows it in a plain text line beside the army number.

label: Has acclaimed knights
summary: Whether the army has any acclaimed knights.
details: The army window uses it to show the parts about them.

label: Has event troops
summary: Whether the army has troops that came from an event.
details: The army window uses it with the hired troops list to decide what to show.

label: Has looter stance
summary: Whether the army is set to the looter stance.
details: The army window uses it as the state of a checkbox.

label: Is suffering attrition
summary: Whether the army is currently losing troops to attrition.
details: The outliner and the shared tooltip use it to show a warning part.

label: Is barter army
summary: Whether the army is on a barter mission.
details: The map icons and the army window use it to show barter parts.
